chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who leads a group in prayer wearing only a shirt, without a cloak upon him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting unless there is upon him a cloak or a turban, with which he covers himself.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum clothing requirement for a man leading Salat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the minimum attire for a male imam leading congregational prayer, requiring either a rida' (upper cloak) or an imamah (turban) to ensure adequate coverage beyond a simple qamis. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the importance of dignified appearance (hay'ah) during worship, distinguishing the leader's attire from that of a solitary pray-er. The emphasis on the rida' or imamah reflects the scholarly view that these garments provide sufficient coverage for the upper body while maintaining the modesty required for leading the community.
